expectedBehaviors: Every durable memory event remains represented as a namespaced graph node with its direct supersession lineage and bounded temporal metadata.

expectedBehaviors: One foreground command exposes the existing repository MCP resources and tools on a fixed loopback interface with a documented health endpoint.
HTTP requests are bounded, stateless, DNS-rebinding resistant, origin checked, and isolated without introducing authentication or remote-host claims.
Existing stdio MCP, managed client configs, the portable runtime, and the optional Python governed store retain their current behavior.

features.featureDescription: Add one explicit CLI-to-intelligence abstraction request using existing authenticated HTTP and env-driven model infrastructure. A strict proposal selects only recorded observations; the CLI preserves full local evidence and writes an incomplete draft after revalidating the source snapshot.
expectedBehaviors: Only explicit capture draft --abstract sends the selected minimized observations and caller goal to the configured authenticated intelligence service; ordinary drafts and hooks stay offline.

A configured model may select recorded observations and suggest a title, triggers, omission reasons, and recovery summary; it cannot supply executable steps, paths, arguments, prerequisites, sources, task receipts, or approval.

All original observations, failures, unknown outcomes, omitted observations, and source evidence remain reviewable in a local incomplete draft; deterministic candidate steps preserve recorded order and tool arguments.
The repository lock is released for the bounded network call, then the complete selected episode and source fingerprints are revalidated under the lock before writing any draft.

Strict shared request and response schemas, canonical hashes, reference partitions, byte limits, deadlines, configured-origin restrictions, authenticated write scope, and generic errors protect both trust boundaries.

Unavailable providers or malformed responses fail without a fake offline abstraction, ledger mutation, or model-key disclosure. Both draft views and temporary paths are preflighted; handled second-file failures restore prior bytes and clean owned temporary payloads. Publication is not crash-atomic and rollback failures require review.
Learning, approval, exact-version outcome receipts, and ready status retain the existing explicit governance gates; model suggestions and successful tool observations never prove task success.

userStories.problemStatement: The portable repo map detects packages and commands, but those observations are only current-state artifacts. They do not create durable history, reconcile changes, or record when an observed workflow disappears.
userStories.featureDescription: Add one deterministic reconciler to the existing refresh generation. It derives package facts and command workflows only from RepoMap, assigns stable logical identities and source fingerprints, and appends ADD, SUPERSEDE, or RETRACT events while unchanged observations produce NOOP. Generated events remain tool-authority, observed, internal, and source-attested.
expectedBehaviors: Each detected package produces one fact candidate and each declared command produces one workflow candidate.
Generated memories cite the manifest path and its scanned SHA-256 and carry stable generator, logical-key, and candidate-fingerprint metadata.

The first observation is added once, an unchanged refresh is byte-for-byte ledger stable, a changed observation supersedes its prior generated head, and a removed observation creates one retraction tombstone.
Incomplete, capped, or unreadable scans may add or supersede observed candidates but defer every apparent deletion until a complete scan confirms it.
The reconciler never generates decisions, preferences, or rationale and never mutates or supersedes manually authored memories.
Higher-authority overrides win; ambiguous generated lineages or reserved-id collisions fail safely before persistence.
The ledger, brain, map, graph, views, and manifest commit as one refresh generation or roll back together.
Refresh output exposes candidate, ADD, NOOP, SUPERSEDE, RETRACT, deferred, conflict, and elapsed-millisecond counters without persisting timing noise.
Session start, installed Git hooks, and the daemon receive the behavior through their existing refreshRepoBrain call path.
acceptanceCriteria: Candidate extraction reads source facts only from RepoMap.packages, RepoMap.commands, and their corresponding RepoFile SHA-256 values; it performs no additional source scan, network call, model call, or database call.

Package candidates use kind fact and command candidates use kind workflow; all generated events use authority tool, provenance method observed, sensitivity internal, and an exact reserved generator marker.

Logical identity is independent of mutable candidate content. Candidate fingerprints are computed from the canonical normalized declaration and source path, while the event separately records the scanned manifest SHA-256; generated event ids are deterministic from logical identity, action, fingerprint, and predecessor, and unrelated edits in the same manifest do not churn unaffected candidates.
A first refresh appends exactly one event per candidate. A second unchanged refresh appends zero bytes, preserves the exact memory fingerprint, and reports every candidate as NOOP.

Changing a manifest-backed observation appends one active successor that supersedes the prior generated head. Removing it appends one retracted successor, repeated absence is a NOOP, and reappearance supersedes the tombstone.
Repo-map scan diagnostics distinguish a complete scan from a capped or unreadable scan; incomplete scans report deferred removals and append no retraction tombstones.
Real observation timestamps are created only when an event is appended and are injectable for deterministic tests; timestamps and duration are not part of candidate identity.
Existing human, agent, and system memories remain byte-identical. No automatic event may use kind decision or preference or contain a rationale field.

A higher-authority successor blocks automatic regeneration for that logical key and increments conflicts without modification. Multiple generated heads, malformed reserved metadata, or a reserved-id collision abort refresh before any file changes.

The pre-existing raw ledger remains an exact byte prefix, including its line-ending style and blank lines, while the final raw ledger is included in the same locked generation and rollback set as derived artifacts; manifest and context fingerprints hash the committed ledger bytes.

expectedBehaviors: The graph is built only after reconciliation and attests both the current repo-map fingerprint and exact committed ledger fingerprint.
Every ledger event becomes one namespaced memory node; code node and edge identifiers remain unchanged.
Direct supersession, source citation, and applicability relationships are represented without dangling endpoints or copying memory bodies and arbitrary structured data into the graph.
Memory nodes expose half-open producer-effective intervals derived in linear time from event createdAt and direct successors.
An explicit memory-as-of timestamp selects the ledger heads effective at that instant while code files, symbols, and imports remain the current repo snapshot.
No as-of input preserves existing deterministic current-head behavior and does not inject the wall clock into generated artifacts.
Context packets expose and render the memory-as-of boundary, retain the full raw-ledger fingerprint, and prevent inactive history from distorting graph ranking.

acceptanceCriteria: Graph schema v2 includes sourceFingerprint, memoryFingerprint, projectionFingerprint, and timeSemantics set to event-effective-time; the memory fingerprint exactly equals SHA-256 of committed raw ledger bytes.
refreshRepoBrain reconciles the final ledger before graph construction, and the graph, manifest, context, and ledger all expose the same memory fingerprint in that generation.
Memory graph IDs are namespaced from event IDs; duplicate node or edge IDs abort construction rather than overwriting another record; all pre-existing code node and edge IDs remain byte-identical.

Each ledger event projects only bounded indexing fields: event id, title, kind, subject type, declared status, authority, confidence, importance, sensitivity, createdAt-derived validFrom, and validTo. Body, arbitrary structuredData, credentials, and raw secret material are not copied into graph metadata.

For an active event, validTo is the earliest createdAt of any direct successor; declared superseded and retracted events encode an empty interval as validTo equal to validFrom, while null is reserved for an open active leaf; intervals are half-open, equal-time successors win at the boundary, and multiple successor branches remain explicit.

Supersedes edges connect successor to predecessor. Citation and applies-to edges resolve only exact current repository/file/symbol targets, with dot resolving to repo root; missing historical paths remain cited in the ledger but create no dangling graph edge.

Temporal interval and reverse-reference construction is O(events plus supersession references), proven by deterministic event-visit and supersession-reference-visit diagnostics plus a large-chain/fan-out smoke. Structural output is independent of RepoMap collection ordering; raw ledger order is an attested input and is never reordered or claimed byte-equivalent.
memoryAsOf accepts only a canonical UTC timestamp in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ form and rejects invalid or hostile input with a generic error that does not reflect the value.

The memory-as-of view uses events created at or before the boundary and the existing active-head rules over that prefix; later appended backdated events may change prior effective views, which is documented as effective-time rather than transaction-time behavior.

ContextQuery and ContextPacket expose memoryAsOf; rendered packets state that memory is as of the selected timestamp while repository topology is current, preserve the full ledger fingerprint, and rank only the induced active-memory graph plus current code topology.

The context CLI supports --memory-as-of, graph queries support --memory-as-of, and graph timeline resolves raw or namespaced memory IDs and returns complete deterministic supersession/retraction lineage.
Existing MCP context, graph-neighbor, and graph-path tools accept the same optional memoryAsOf input and return the same induced graph behavior without adding a redundant server or model call.

Neo4j projection fingerprint is SHA-256 of a canonical tuple containing adapter namespace, projection version, source fingerprint, and memory fingerprint; it drives stale node and edge cleanup and is returned with source and memory fingerprints in sync results.

Graph v1 remains readable as a code-only legacy artifact, algorithms continue to accept v1 and v2, and the next locked refresh regenerates v2 without changing memory-event schema v1, manifest schema v1, or canonical sync bytes.

A pure stored-artifact integrity validator used by the harness rejects mismatched graph/manifest memory fingerprints and malformed temporal endpoints without first repairing them. userStories.featureDescription: Add `provena mcp serve --http [--port <port>]` as an explicit foreground mode. Reuse the existing `createRepoMcpServer` registrations with the bundled `createMcpExpressApp` and `StreamableHTTPServerTransport`, bind only `127.0.0.1`, expose POST `/mcp` and GET `/healthz`, use a fresh stateless JSON-response MCP server and transport per request, and make the same command available from the persisted portable runtime and a freshly installed package.
expectedBehaviors: The explicit foreground command listens on `127.0.0.1:18093` by default, exposes `/mcp` and `/healthz`, and reports the actual URL plus startup duration.
Stdio MCP, managed stdio configs, and the separate Python store command and port remain unchanged.
HTTP exposes the same repository-bound resources and tools as stdio without refreshing at startup.
Each POST uses a fresh stateless JSON-response MCP server and transport; concurrent mutations retain the existing repository lock.
Fixed loopback binding, Host and Origin checks, a 100 KiB body cap, bounded generic errors, and non-cacheable responses protect the unauthenticated local endpoint.
SIGINT and SIGTERM close the foreground listener without durable HTTP state or orphaned processes.
The persisted runtime and packed installation serve HTTP offline from bundled dependencies.
Documentation distinguishes this local-process trust boundary from authenticated remote and enterprise MCP.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI help documents `provena mcp serve --http [--port <port>]`; default is 18093; exactly one canonical base-10 port from 1 through 65535 is accepted, and invalid or unknown input fails generically.
Without `--http`, stdio remains silent and listener-free; `mcp install` keeps stdio configs; top-level `provena serve` still owns the optional Python store on 18092.

HTTP has no host option and binds only `127.0.0.1`; bind collision fails promptly. GET `/healthz` returns bounded non-sensitive JSON, POST `/mcp` is the only MCP route, known wrong methods return 405, and unknown routes return 404.

Bundled `createMcpExpressApp({ host: "127.0.0.1" })` and `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` are used. Each POST gets a fresh server/transport with no session ID generator and `enableJsonResponse: true`, closes in a finally path, and exposes no GET SSE or DELETE session flow.

A real HTTP MCP client can initialize, list the same five tools, read brain/map/graph/manifest, and call read and mutation tools with stdio-equivalent behavior. Git root is fixed at startup, requests cannot override it, and concurrent mutations use the existing lock.

Missing, malformed, or non-local Host is rejected. Origin may be absent; when present it must exactly match `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, `http://localhost:<port>`, or `http://[::1]:<port>`; other origins receive 403 and no permissive CORS header.

JSON bodies are capped at 100 KiB before MCP parsing. All responses include `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; bounded 4xx/5xx errors and logs never echo bodies, headers, hostile values, stack traces, absolute repo paths, memory content, environment values, or credentials.

The programmatic start result and one CLI startup line expose actual host, port, MCP URL, and finite nonnegative monotonic `startupMs`. Foreground SIGINT/SIGTERM closes the listener, releases the port, and leaves no pid, session, token, or database state.

Generated `runtime.mjs` delegates `mcp serve --http` to its installed `@provena/cli`. Fresh packed CLI and persisted-runtime tests complete a real HTTP MCP exchange offline without source, Python, Docker, model access, or another registry call.

README, CLI README, Quickstart, and architecture docs cover command, URL, health, shutdown, and threat model: any local process can invoke read and mutation tools. userStories.userStory: As a developer, I want each normal Provena refresh to compile deterministic maintenance tasks and cited task contexts so agents can review evidence gaps, stale references, and exact duplicates without granting an autonomous process permission to mutate durable memory.
userStories.problemStatement: The repository brain refreshes current topology and source-grounded package and workflow memories, but it does not yet expose bounded review work for unsupported memories, missing current paths, or exact duplicate active claims. Calling this dreaming or subagent coordination without a durable deterministic proposal contract would overstate the product and create an unsafe self-modification boundary.
userStories.featureDescription: Add a manifest-attested `.provena/maintenance.plan.json` derived only from the committed RepoMap and canonical ledger heads. The compiler emits capped evidence-gap, source-not-in-map, scope-not-in-map, and exact-content-overlap issues plus deterministic review tasks. CLI and MCP read the plan and compile exact-memory, exact-path, cited, token-bounded context packets suitable for delegation, but never spawn processes, approve proposals, or write ledger events.
expectedBehaviors: Every refresh generation deterministically regenerates the maintenance plan from the same source and exact-ledger snapshots used by the graph and manifest.
The plan identifies active memories without evidence, references absent from a complete current map, scopes absent from a complete current map, and exact normalized active-memory overlaps.
Incomplete scans defer every absence-based source and scope issue rather than turning partial visibility into stale-memory advice.
Exact overlap detection is linear in active events plus references and never performs pairwise semantic comparison or a model call.
The plan is compact, bounded, non-sensitive, and carries stable issue and task identities plus source, memory, and plan fingerprints.
Maintenance remains proposal-only: generating, reading, or compiling a task context never appends, supersedes, retracts, approves, or deletes a memory.
CLI users can list plan tasks, compile one task context, and request exact memories in ordinary context packets.
Stdio and loopback HTTP MCP expose the same maintenance plan and context operations through the existing repository-bound server.
Session start, Git hooks, daemon ticks, manual refresh, and installed runtimes inherit plan regeneration through the existing refresh path without a new scheduler or service.
acceptanceCriteria: `.provena/maintenance.plan.json` joins the exact managed artifact set, is committed before the manifest in the same locked rollback-capable generation, and is covered by manifest hash/byte declarations plus the existing per-artifact and aggregate read caps.

Plan schema v1 records planner namespace and integer version, sourceFingerprint, exact raw-ledger memoryFingerprint, planFingerprint, scanComplete, truncated, summary counters, issues, and tasks. planFingerprint hashes one canonical self-excluding payload and the stored plan must exactly equal a canonical recomputation before consumption.

Only canonical active memory heads are inspected. Evidence-gap means both sources and appliesTo are empty; source-not-in-map uses missing source paths; scope-not-in-map uses missing appliesTo paths except dot; and exact-content-overlap groups two or more events by kind, subject type, normalized title, normalized body, and normalized appliesTo.

When RepoMap.scan.complete is false, source-not-in-map and scope-not-in-map checks produce no issues, increment a bounded deferred-path-check count, and leave evidence-gap and exact-overlap checks deterministic.

Overlap indexing and reference inspection visit each active event, source, and scope a bounded number of times, expose deterministic diagnostics for tests, and do not use embeddings, edit distance, all-pairs comparison, network, database, filesystem rescan, or model inference.

The compiler emits at most 256 issues and 256 tasks, each record carries at most 32 sorted unique memory IDs and 32 normalized repo-relative paths, serialized plan size is at most 512 KiB, and deterministic truncation plus summary counters disclose omitted work.

The plan never copies memory title, body, structuredData, provenance actor, agent, session, command, environment values, source snippets, credentials, or arbitrary user content. It contains only fixed planner text, enum values, IDs, repo-relative paths, fingerprints, versions, booleans, and numeric counters and passes the secret-material guard.

Plan generation and reads preserve exact ledger bytes and memory fingerprint. userStories.title: Abstract selected coding-tool observations into reviewable procedure drafts
userStories.persona: Developer who wants reusable procedures grounded in real coding-tool observations
userStories.userStory: As a developer, I want to explicitly request a bounded model abstraction of selected observations so I can review a reusable procedure without granting the model authority to invent actions, declare success, or approve durable memory.
userStories.problemStatement: Capture currently records minimized observations and creates deterministic drafts, but cannot propose relevant steps and triggers from a longer episode. Model output needs a narrow grounded contract so unsupported actions and outcome claims cannot enter a procedure.
userStories.featureDescription: Add one explicit CLI-to-intelligence abstraction request using existing authenticated HTTP and env-driven model infrastructure. A strict proposal selects only recorded observations; the CLI preserves full local evidence and writes an incomplete draft after revalidating the source snapshot.
expectedBehaviors: Only explicit capture draft --abstract sends the selected minimized observations and caller goal to the configured authenticated intelligence service; ordinary drafts and hooks stay offline.

A configured model may select recorded observations and suggest a title, triggers, omission reasons, and recovery summary; it cannot supply executable steps, paths, arguments, prerequisites, sources, task receipts, or approval.

All original observations, failures, unknown outcomes, omitted observations, and source evidence remain reviewable in a local incomplete draft; deterministic candidate steps preserve recorded order and tool arguments.
The repository lock is released for the bounded network call, then the complete selected episode and source fingerprints are revalidated under the lock before writing any draft.

Strict shared request and response schemas, canonical hashes, reference partitions, byte limits, deadlines, configured-origin restrictions, authenticated write scope, and generic errors protect both trust boundaries.

Unavailable providers or malformed responses fail without a fake offline abstraction, ledger mutation, or model-key disclosure. Both draft views and temporary paths are preflighted; handled second-file failures restore prior bytes and clean owned temporary payloads. Publication is not crash-atomic and rollback failures require review.
Learning, approval, exact-version outcome receipts, and ready status retain the existing explicit governance gates; model suggestions and successful tool observations never prove task success.
acceptanceCriteria: The CLI exposes an explicit --abstract flag on capture draft and rejects malformed flags. The configured intelligence_url points to the authenticated gateway origin in production; existing client bearer and scope helpers are reused. No model-provider credential is sent by the CLI.

POST /v1/procedures/abstract is routed through the authenticated gateway with write authorization and authoritative service identity; the intelligence service validates ingress and write authority before parsing/model work. Direct external client bearers are rejected. Request schemaVersion is integer 1, goal is bounded, observations contain at most 32 hashed IDs and safe argument/status/issue fields, and unknown fields are rejected.

The request stream is limited to 256 KiB before parsing. Model response content is bounded to 80 KiB with a total deadline on the new transport path; compressed expansion, redirects, provider failures, missing model configuration, and invalid JSON fail generically.

Model output contains only bounded title, triggers, a nonempty unique keptObservationIds subset, an exact complementary omission partition with reasons, and recoverySummary. Unknown/duplicate IDs and invented commands/paths/arguments/prerequisites/outcomes are rejected.

inputSha256 hashes the strict normalized complete request using UTF-8 compact sorted-key JSON without a trailing newline. outputSha256 hashes the full response except outputSha256, including input hash, prompt revision, and configured model metadata. Type, Unicode, and goal-trim parity are tested across Python and TypeScript.

Before the call, a locked validated snapshot includes the entire episode and selected current source fingerprints. After the call, a fresh locked read must match; changed sources, changed or removed episode data, nested repositories, symlinks, tracked/unignored cache targets, or unsafe paths fail without writing a draft.

Candidate goal remains the explicit caller goal and explicit caller title takes precedence. Candidate steps/arguments are derived only from recorded selected observations in original order. Model recovery text and configured model metadata remain untrusted local wrapper data; deterministic failure warnings and all original evidence remain.

Every draft remains complete=false, taskOutcome=unknown, verification=[], and unapproved; abstraction never executes commands or writes the authoritative memory ledger. Existing learn/approve/outcome gates are exercised by focused regressions.

Use only existing Node/Zod/fetch and FastAPI/Pydantic/httpx/model router/shared LLM client dependencies, with env-driven model selection. Existing callers retain their previous LLM transport behavior.

Focused lifecycle, authorization, no-network-default, adversarial input/output, concurrency, transport caps, and full CLI/intelligence/E2E checks pass on the final source. Documentation states configured-model metadata limits, opt-in egress, and draft-only status. Actual provider/task-quality and competitor results remain explicitly pending until measured.
